title: Top Sellers
statement: A store with 5,000,000 products shows the 20 best-selling products on its home page, from a list of each product's sales count.
examples: Return the 20 product IDs with the highest sales

approaches.name: A min-heap of size 20 over all products
approaches.hint: Keep only the current best k
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Each product costs O(log 20); the heap never grows past 20 items.

approaches.name: Sort all products by sales and take the first 20
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct, but it orders 5,000,000 items when only 20 matter.

approaches.name: Scan for the maximum 20 times, removing it each time
approaches.hint: Find the best, then the next best
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct and fine for k = 20, but it grows linearly with k.

approaches.name: Take the first 20 products in the list
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: The list is not ordered by sales, so the first 20 are not the best sellers.

title: Merge News Feeds
statement: A reader follows 500 news sources. Each source gives its stories already sorted by time. Build one timeline sorted by time from all 2,000,000 stories.
examples: Three sorted feeds become one sorted timeline

approaches.name: K-way merge with a min-heap of each feed's next story
approaches.hint: Compare only the front of each list
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: The heap holds one story per feed; each story is pushed and popped once at a cost of log 500.

approaches.name: Join all feeds and sort the result
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct, but it ignores that each feed is already sorted.

approaches.name: Merge the feeds two at a time, one after another
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct, but early stories are copied again in every later merge.

approaches.name: Take one story from each feed in turn
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Taking turns ignores the times, so the timeline is not sorted.

title: Charging Bays
statement: Electric buses arrive at a depot with fixed charging start and end times. Find the fewest charging bays so that no two buses share a bay at the same time.

approaches.name: Sort by start; min-heap of end times of busy bays
approaches.hint: Reuse the bay that frees up first
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: The heap root is the bay that frees up earliest, so each bus either reuses it or opens a new bay.

approaches.name: Sort starts and ends separately and sweep with two pointers
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Also correct and just as fast; it counts how many buses charge at each start time.

approaches.name: Compare every pair of buses for overlap
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Counting overlapping pairs does not give the number of bays, and it is too slow for 100,000 buses.
